content:
ops-bot: INCIDENT: detected elevated 5xx rate and request latency from AWS AP-NORTHEAST-3 region impacting Hosted API and several Dedicated pools. Automatic page sent to rotation. Metrics: 5xx spike ~18% over baseline, p95 latency up from 110ms to ~1.4s.

maria: I'm on it — taking initial triage. Which teams are seeing the Dedicated pool errors?

devraj: confirmed for dp-pool-42 and dp-pool-7 (tokyo-ish racks). Hosted API frontends in ap-northeast-3 also showing 502/504.

sam: logs show STS token refresh errors for a subset of worker nodes: ``error: sts assume-role failed: 503 Service Unavailable``. Also seeing elevated ALB 5xx counts.

lee: AWS status page (https://status.aws.amazon.com/) shows degraded STS in ap-northeast-3, and a related ELB surge. Opening a support ticket now.

support-bot: AWS case #135790 opened by lee: "ELB/STS increased error rate in ap-northeast-3 causing token failures and backend 5xx".

maria: immediate mitigations — 1) Stop scheduling new jobs to affected Dedicated pools (dp-pool-42/7). 2) Enable regional fallback routing for Hosted API traffic to ap-northeast-1 and ap-northeast-2 for latency-tolerant requests. 3) Shorten token TTL to force fresh STS paths (workaround for caching issue).

devraj: I'm running a canary reroute for ~5% of traffic to ap-northeast-2 now via routing-policy `regional-fanout-v2` — monitoring error rate.

sam: canary looks good so far — errors on canary <1%. Metrics team please watch error budget.

lee: Ops note: we need to preserve low-latency SLOs for enterprise customers. Will only route standard calls; premium/low-latency pinned customers keep their regional reservation if possible.

maria: @support-bot please draft a short status blurb for customers: product impact, mitigation steps, ETA estimate. Keep it conservative.

support-bot: Draft: "We are seeing elevated errors and latency for API requests routed through AWS ap-northeast-3 due to a third-party cloud service disruption. We are routing affected traffic to adjacent regions and limiting new job scheduling in affected Dedicated pools. We will provide updates every 30 minutes."

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: maria acknowledged the incident, devraj and sam are responders, SRE escalation queued to sre-lead.

maria: SRE-lead, can you confirm if we should evict KV caches for ap-northeast-3 nodes? There may be cached STS tokens.

sre-lead: Evicting entire regional prefix cache is risky. Suggest rolling restart of affected nodes + targeted KV prefix purge for auth tokens (prefix `sts-cache/ap-northeast-3/*`). Devraj, coordinate.

devraj: Starting targeted purge on dp-pool-42 in 1 minute. Command snippet (run on control plane):

```
curl -X POST -H \"Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN\" https://control-plane.internal/kv/purge \
  -d '{"prefix":"sts-cache/ap-northeast-3/","region":"ap-northeast-3"}'
```

sam: Purge kicked off, watching logs. Token-related 5xx are dropping on purge by ~30% for dp-pool-42. Good sign.

maria: Good. Now schedule rolling restart for worker nodes with fresh STS handshake. Keep two nodes up at all times.

lee: I've throttled new enrollment tasks and put a temporary limit on batch inference in the region. This will reduce load on ELB and STS.

support-bot: Support playbook update note: instruct support to inform customers that some in-region Dedicated pools may show degraded throughput; recommend failover to cross-region pools if acceptable.

maria: Customer impact assessment — preliminary: ~4% of Hosted API requests experienced errors during the spike window, impacting ~20 small-mid customers with burst traffic patterns. Two enterprise customers with Dedicated pools in ap-northeast-3 saw degraded throughput and delayed responses. No confirmed data exfiltration.

devraj: Alerting for billing/usage anomalies triggered for a couple of customers — likely retries causing higher token usage. We'll flag for billing review after the incident.

sam: Monitoring shows p95 latency back to ~200ms on rerouted traffic; 5xx reduced from 18% to ~3% overall after mitigation steps. Still higher than baseline, but improving.

ops-bot: Event marker: mitigation-phase-start 3621234980.

maria: We should post an internal postmortem stub: timeline, root cause (third-party STS/ELB partial regional degradation), mitigations (routing fallback, token purge, rolling restarts), customer impact, follow-ups (hardening routing, increase cross-region fallback cadence). @sre-lead to own RCA.

sre-lead: Acknowledged. I'll assign RCA and follow-ups. Immediate follow-ups: add health-check for STS client errors to trigger automatic cross-region routing earlier; investigate token cache TTL policy.

lee: Drafting status page update now with the support-bot blurb + ETA. Propose next update in 30 minutes.

support-bot: Status page update posted: "We are continuing to route impacted traffic away from ap-northeast-3; partial service degradation may continue as AWS works on the upstream issue. Next update in 30 minutes."

maria: Handing incident to on-call SRE for monitoring and RCA — I'll remain available. @sre-lead please take over incident channel.

sre-lead: Taking over. Continuing to monitor, will compile initial RCA notes. Current plan: monitor for 2 hours, then start postmortem draft.

ops-bot: Incident resolved: AWS reports recovery for STS and ELB in ap-northeast-3. Metrics stable. Closing page in 2h unless regression. Event marker: mitigation-phase-end 3621236799.

maria: Closing notes — good coordination, targeted purge + reroute worked well. Follow-ups: schedule runbook update for `regional-fallback` to include STS-specific failures and token purge steps.

support-bot: Customer follow-up: support to send targeted messages to affected Dedicated customers with recommended actions and mitigation timeline.

sre-lead: I'll kick off the postmortem doc and add action items with owners.

sam: leaving a quick log snippet for SRE doc: ``ALB_5xx: spike=18pct; STS_err: assume-role 503; action: purge-sts-cache -> +roll restarts -> reroute -> restore``

maria: thanks all. I'll archive incident artifacts into the incidents bucket and tag RCA.
